title: Blind stroke-sculpt run on the user's skull: sculptor sees only Ixdar-rendered reference pictures, judge sees only chamfer
description:
A blind run of stroke sculpting on the user's skull, following the stroke-sculpt skill (ai-workspace .claude/skills/stroke-sculpt). It measures how far the tools get from reference pictures alone, without the goal mesh or a score to hill-climb, as in real use. Compare it with MESH-68 (0.0170 chamfer with goal renders, traced goal outlines and chamfer feedback).

- Orchestrator (the main session): the goal is in ~/.cache/ixdar-sculpt-judge/skull/, never in a worktree. Render the references through Ixdar with the skill's render_references.py (orbit-set --fov --roll, from MESH-70) into the sculptor's worktree tmp/references/, with a new seed. Check the pictures, then brief a fresh sculptor agent that has never seen the goal.
- Sculptor: sees only tmp/references/*.png and its own sculpt. It builds resources/dsl/skull/ as chained stroke_sculpt passes, judges each pass against the pictures in tmp/passes.md, and stops on its own judgement or at the pass limit (12).
- Judge: a separate agent that sees only the sculptor's DSL and the goal mesh, never a picture. It measures the chamfer floor and scores every pass headless into the judge directory.
- The result replaces master's broken stroke_sculpt_skull.dsl. That file loads an OBJ that never landed because *.obj is gitignored.
definition-of-done:
1. The reference set is rendered through Ixdar only (no Blender) with the run's seed recorded in the judge directory's manifest.
2. The sculptor's worktree never contains the goal mesh, a manifest or a score; its report confirms it found none.
3. A chained-pass skull DSL under resources/dsl/skull/ with every pass SVG tracked (nothing gitignored), replacing stroke_sculpt_skull.dsl, opened by a launch.json entry.
4. The judge's scores-<run>.json holds the floor and chamfer/Hausdorff per pass; the final numbers and MESH-68's 0.0170 are compared in the ticket's changes-made.
5. The sculptor's tmp/passes.md and a final multiview next to the references are under tmp/.
testing-plan:
1. Before briefing: open every reference picture and confirm the jitter, FOV spread and framing look like a real reference set.
2. After the run: the judge re-evaluates the final DSL headless and in the viewer and gets the same chamfer.
3. grep the sculptor's worktree and transcript summary for the judge directory path and goal file names; there must be no hit.
unknowns: Does the sculptor get the pass limit only, or also a time budget?
changes-made: Added ixdar-app/src/main/resources/dsl/skull/skull.dsl plus pass1.svg-pass9.svg: sphere(size 2, res 64) -> 9 stroke_sculpt passes (symmetry x, strength 1) -> subdivision_surface(levels 1), drawn blind from tmp/references only. Passes: 1-4 outline and proportion (front, side, top silhouettes, lower back cut, occiput step), 5 orbits and nasal aperture, 6 brow, nasal bridge, cheek hollow, zygomatic arch, temporal fossa, 7 bite line and teeth, 8 chin and under-occiput outline, 9 hollow under the arch and mandible border.
Added launch.json entry 'Mesh Node Viewer: stroke-sculpt skull' (plain name, kept on land) opening dsl/skull/skull.dsl in mesh-viewer.
Not reached by strokes: ear canal, the opening between ramus and maxilla, mastoids (stroke_sculpt displaces, it cannot cut holes); socket and fossa rims terrace at the local refinement edge.

Tool gap found: the multiview --svg template's own comment contains a literal polyline tag that StrokeSketch's regex parser reads as a stroke, so the DSL fails with 'For input string: x' while ixdar-cli model still reports ok; each template comment was reworded by hand.

Sculptor artifacts under tmp/: subject.md, passes.md, captures/, animation/ (sculpt-animate frames, mp4, gif), final_vs_references.png. Judge scores and the comparison with MESH-68's 0.0170 are for the judge/orchestrator to add; master's stroke_sculpt_skull.dsl was not touched by the sculptor.

Judge (blind, numbers only), against the 57k goal with mesh-compare --normalize. Floor 0.00216 chamfer / 0.0046 Hausdorff. Chamfer by pass: sphere 0.0498, then 0.0488, 0.0409, 0.0343, 0.0323, 0.0277, 0.0268, 0.0256, 0.0247, 0.0246; final skull.dsl (with subdivision) 0.0238, Hausdorff 0.166. Chamfer fell every pass and levelled off at 8-9. MESH-68 reached 0.0170 with the goal's renders and chamfer feedback; blind is about 40% higher, closing 52% of the start-to-floor gap against MESH-68's 68%. The orientation of goal and sculpt agrees (both face +z, y up). The sculpt is too wide for its height: width:height 0.82 against the goal's 0.72.
Archived 2026-10-31 without landing, as tag archive/mesh-72 at 7ea2a548: Blind run 1: sculptor stopped itself after 9 passes, chamfer 0.0238; rerun under the revised stroke-sculpt protocol
review-summary: A sphere is sculpted blind into a skull by nine chained stroke_sculpt passes in dsl/skull/skull.dsl, drawn only from the reference pictures. It is the replacement for the broken stroke_sculpt_skull.dsl demo and gives the judge a pass-by-pass DSL to score.
